ed.title: Edibles & cannabutter calculator
ed.noteEstimate: Estimates. The actual dose can differ considerably.
ed.noteOnset: Edibles: onset 30 min – 2 h, do not redose.
ed.modeTotalHint: Value from the label (“Total THC”) – already includes converted THCA
ed.modeSplitHint: Lab values for Δ9-THC and THCA separately
ed.totalNote: “Total THC” already includes the converted THCA – the factor 0.877 is not applied again.
ed.uncertaintyHint: Studies often find label values to deviate considerably (Schwabe et al. 2023).
ed.alreadyDecarbedHint: e.g. material that was already heated, or distillate – then there are no decarboxylation losses.
ed.decarbHint: Share of THCA retained as THC (incomplete conversion + degradation). Uncertainty ± 10 pp.
ed.extractHint: Share of THC that passes into the fat. There are no reliable standard values for home methods. Uncertainty ± 15 pp.
ed.strainLossHint: Fat that stays in the plant material. Does not change the concentration – only the available amount.
ed.recipeSub: How much butter goes into how many portions?
ed.resultSub: Estimates with a range – not exact values
ed.lossSub: From theoretical content to butter (mean values)
ed.curveTitle: Dose per portion by amount of cannabis
ed.curveSub: Green band = uncertainty range, line = mean
ed.lossNote: Each loss is applied exactly once. The straining loss only reduces the amount of butter, not its concentration.
ed.reverseSub: How much cannabis for a desired calculated dose per portion?
ed.needHint: Range: in case the material is stronger (less needed) or weaker (more needed) than assumed. If in doubt, choose the smaller amount.
ed.needThc: Please enter a THC content greater than 0.
ed.reverseHint: With {n} portions, {a} g butter in the recipe and {b} g butter in total.
ed.wRatio: Very high cannabis-to-fat ratio: the fat may be saturated or soaked up by the plant material – extraction is then probably lower.
ed.wFat: The recipe needs {need} g butter/oil, but only about {have} g is available after straining.

dose.startText: Matches Health Canada's recommendation for starting out (≤ 2.5 mg). Effects are possible even here – especially without tolerance.
dose.lowText: Up to one "Standard THC Unit" (5 mg). Already noticeable for inexperienced users; do not redose before the full effect is reached.
dose.moderateText: Up to the Canadian maximum per edible package (10 mg). People without tolerance may experience unpleasant effects.
dose.highText: Above the Health Canada package limit. Clearly increased risk of anxiety, racing heart, nausea and strong impairment – especially with low tolerance.
dose.veryHighText: A multiple of the starting dose. High likelihood of strong, long-lasting effects; not advisable without marked tolerance.
dose.extremeText: Very high amounts can cause acute overdose with panic, confusion, vomiting, circulatory problems or psychotic symptoms. In an emergency, get medical help.
dose.wUncertainty: The uncertainty is large: the actual dose can be more than twice the mean.
dose.wOverdose: Considerable risk of overdose. Effects can last more than 12 hours.
dose.fact1: When smoking, only part of the THC reaches the bloodstream (typically about 10–35 %). When eating, it is only about 4–12 % – yet edibles often act more strongly and for longer.
dose.fact2: The reason is liver metabolism: orally ingested THC is increasingly converted into 11-hydroxy-THC, which is itself psychoactive.
dose.fact3: Edibles act with a delay (30 min to 2 h) and considerably longer (up to 12 h, residual effects up to 24 h).
dose.fact4: A mg figure for a joint (theoretical content) and for an edible (amount ingested) describe fundamentally different things.
dose.wPackage: The possible upper limit ({high} mg) is at or above {limit} mg – the maximum Health Canada allows for a whole edible package.
dose.wStart: For beginners, Health Canada recommends at most {n} mg THC. Consider eating only part of the portion.

factor.toleranceText: Regular use leads to tolerance to many THC effects. It drops again after breaks – previous amounts may then be too strong.
factor.bodyText: Body weight, body fat, liver metabolism (CYP enzymes) and genetics considerably affect THC uptake and breakdown.
factor.stomachText: With edibles, meals and fat content change absorption. Onset can be delayed and the effect can be stronger or weaker.
factor.mixingText: Alcohol and other substances increase impairment. Interactions with medication are possible.
factor.setText: Mood, expectations and surroundings shape the experience. Pre-existing mental health conditions increase the risk of unpleasant reactions.
factor.riskText: According to the LRCUG, adolescents, pregnant and breastfeeding people and people with a (family) history of psychosis should avoid cannabis.

val.over100: THC + THCA adds up to more than 100 % – please check the values.
val.needThc: Please enter the THC or THCA content.
val.thcPositive: THC content must be greater than 0.
val.portionsInt: Portions must be a whole number.
val.peopleInt: People must be a whole number.

pot.lowText: Rather low THC content – comparable to older or CBD-rich strains.
pot.midText: Medium THC content, roughly in the range of today's averages.
pot.highText: Above-average THC content. Even small amounts can have strong effects.
pot.veryHighText: Very high THC content. Higher THC content is associated with a higher risk of acute and long-term harm (LRCUG).
pot.extremeText: Values above ~35 % are unusual for flower and typical of concentrates/extracts. Please check the value.

sm.srcOccasional: Lindgren et al. 1981: occasional users approx. 10 ± 7 %
sm.srcRegular: Lindgren et al. 1981: regular users approx. 23 ± 16 %
sm.pyroText: Part of the THC is destroyed by heat in the ember before it can be inhaled.
sm.sideText: The joint keeps burning between puffs; this smoke is not inhaled.
sm.sideMag: Strongly depends on pauses between puffs and burn time
sm.buttText: THC condenses in the back of the joint, in the filter or tip, and is often thrown away.
sm.buttMag: Variable; depends on the unsmoked remainder
sm.exhaledText: Not all inhaled smoke releases its THC in the lungs; some is exhaled again.
sm.exhaledMag: Depends on puff volume, breath-holding and technique
sm.techniqueText: Experienced users typically absorb more THC per joint than inexperienced ones.
sm.tolNone: Without tolerance, even small amounts of THC can cause marked effects and side effects (anxiety, racing heart, dizziness).
sm.tolLow: Low tolerance: the reaction to THC is hard to predict – dose carefully.
sm.tolMid: Medium tolerance reduces some effects but does not protect against impaired driving ability or concentration.
sm.tolHigh: High tolerance results from frequent use and is associated with an increased risk of dependence. Tolerance decreases during breaks – be careful after a break.
sm.noteTheoretical: The theoretical THC content is NOT the amount absorbed. The systemically available amount is usually much smaller and varies greatly between individuals.
sm.noteSharing: Sharing assumes an even split. In practice, the number and depth of puffs can differ considerably.

tl.smOnsetText: First effects after seconds to a few minutes.
tl.smPeakText: Strongest effect typically around 30 minutes after use.
tl.smDeclineText: The effect wears off; in total it can last up to 6 hours.
tl.smAfterText: Residual effects (e.g. on reaction time) possible for up to 24 hours.
tl.smWarning: Reaction time and attention can be impaired even after noticeable effects have worn off. Do not drive or operate machinery.
tl.edOnsetText: First effects after 30 minutes to 2 hours – sometimes later.
tl.edPeakText: Strongest effect typically around 4 hours after ingestion.
tl.edDeclineText: The effect wears off slowly; up to 12 hours in total.
tl.edAfterText: Residual effects possible for up to 24 hours.
tl.edWarning: Most common mistake: redosing because "nothing is happening yet". The effect can take up to 2 hours (or longer) to appear. Wait at least the full onset time before using again.

smk.title: Joint & smoking calculator
smk.segLow: Lower end of the assumption (not a guaranteed minimum)
smk.restHint: The rest (butt, went out, thrown away) is not taken into account.
smk.profileSub: Only changes the literature range and the notes
smk.tolHint: Tolerance does not change the calculated mg. It affects the effect, not the uptake.
smk.sTheoHint: Whole joint, purely calculated from amount × potency.
smk.where: Where does the THC go? (per person, rough)
smk.lossesSub: Orders of magnitude from the literature – not exact values
smk.timingSub: Typical time ranges according to Health Canada
smk.spanHint: Very rough range from {lo}–{hi} bioavailability (literature). Values outside it are also possible.
smk.threeValues: The three values describe different things and must not be equated. Even the lower end of the range is not a guaranteed minimum – individual uptake can be lower or higher.
smk.varA: In studies, bioavailability from smoking ranged from about 2 to 56 % (Huestis 2007). For these inputs that would be
smk.varB: Puff technique, breath-holding, pauses and experience make a big difference.

da.edibleSub: Cautious reference ranges for orally ingested THC
da.refSub: For orientation, not dosing advice. Basis: Health Canada, standard THC unit
da.vsSub: Why mg figures are not comparable
da.theory: In theory, {a} g of this flower contains {mgA} mg THC, 1 g contains {mgB} mg. How much of it is absorbed depends strongly on the route of use. The classification is not official.
da.overdoseText: Because the effect only starts after 30 minutes to 2 hours, people often take more. This can lead to an unintentionally high dose that lasts many hours. Homemade edibles are particularly unreliable because the THC content per portion can vary widely.
da.emergency: With severe symptoms: calm surroundings, do not stay alone. In case of impaired consciousness, chest pain or severe psychological symptoms, call emergency services (EU: 112). Store edibles out of reach of children and separately from food.

tools.noDilution: Target concentration is not lower – no dilution needed.
tools.ratioSub: Calculate the ratio or determine the amount of fat
tools.reverseSub: How much finished cannabutter for a target dose per portion?
tools.fatFor: Amount of fat for {v} g cannabis
tools.ratioHint: The ratio alone says little about strength – THC content and yields are what matter. A lot of plant material in little fat soaks up the fat and reduces extraction.
tools.fillHint: Make up the rest of the fat in the recipe with regular butter. Since the actual concentration is uncertain, the real dose can differ considerably.

tlv.subtitle: Schematic view of typical time ranges according to Health Canada. The curve height is relative – not a prediction of effect strength.
tlv.band: Band = range between early and late typical course · schematic, not individual

src.hcEffects: Health Canada. Health effects of cannabis. Government of Canada. (Onset, peak, duration and residual effects for inhalation vs. ingestion).
src.hcInfo: Health Canada. Cannabis information, including guidance on edible cannabis (“start low and go slow”; start with products containing ≤ 2.5 mg THC). Government of Canada – landing page, linking to the sub-pages.
src.uStart: Starting dose 2.5 mg, warning about delayed onset
src.regs: Government of Canada. Cannabis Regulations, SOR/2018-144 – maximum of 10 mg THC per package of edible cannabis.
src.uBio: Bioavailability smoking (approx. 10–35 %) and oral (approx. 4–12 %), pyrolysis loss
src.uLabel: Uncertainty of THC values on labels
src.uEdibles: Risks of edibles (delayed onset, overdose, dosing inaccuracy)

fm.total: Total THC from THC and THCA
fm.totalE: 0.877 is the ratio of the molar masses of THC (314.47 g/mol) and THCA (358.48 g/mol). If the label already states “Total THC”, the factor is not applied again.
fm.theoE: The maximum possible amount with complete decarboxylation and no loss at all.
fm.decarbE: η_decarb only applies to the THCA share. If the split is unknown (total THC only), η_decarb is applied to the total – in flower, THC is mostly present as THCA.
fm.fat: THC in the fat and concentration
fm.fatF: mg_fat = mg_decarb × η_extraction;   c = mg_fat ÷ g_fat
fm.fatE: η_extraction is the share that passes into the whole fat phase. Fat that stays in the plant material when straining has the same concentration – it only reduces the amount recovered. This way losses are not counted twice.
fm.recipeF: mg_recipe = c × g_butter_in_recipe;   mg_portion = mg_recipe ÷ portions
fm.recipeE: An even distribution in the dough is assumed – in practice, the content varies between portions.
fm.uncF: low = mg × (1 − u) × η_min…;   high = mg × (1 + u) × η_max…
fm.uncE: u = relative uncertainty of the THC value; η_decarb ± 10 percentage points and η_extraction ± 15 percentage points (limited to 0–100 %). All factors are set unfavourably or favourably at the same time – a conservative worst/best case, not a statistical confidence interval.
fm.revF: g_cannabis = (c_target × g_fat) ÷ (THC yield per g cannabis)
fm.revE: c_target results from target mg per portion × portions ÷ g butter in the recipe.
fm.smokeE: F is the bioavailability. In studies it varies between about 2 and 56 %. The result is a very rough order of magnitude, not a measurement.

asm.decarbB: Assumption; nearly complete under lab conditions (Wang et al. 2016), household ovens vary widely.
asm.extractB: Assumption; no reliable standard values for home methods.
asm.label: THC label uncertainty
asm.labelB: Based on Schwabe et al. 2023 (declared values often too high).

srcv.noMedicalText: This app is an information and calculation tool for harm reduction. It does not replace medical or pharmaceutical advice and does not give dosing recommendations. Laws on possession, cultivation and use differ from country to country.
